He played college basketball for the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs basketball|Mississippi State Bulldogs]]. ==High school career== Sword played high school basketball for [[George Washington Carver High School (Montgomery, Alabama)|George Washington Carver High School]] in [[Montgomery, Alabama|Montgomery]]. His senior year, Sword led his team to the 6A state championship was named [[Alabama Mr. Basketball]]. Sword was listed as 4-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], and choose to attend Mississippi State over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], and [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]].{{Cite web|url = https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Craig-Sword-102423|title = Craig Sword|date = |accessdate = May 22, 2015|website = Rivals.com|publisher = Rivals|last = |first = }} While Sword committed to head coach [[Rick Stansbury]], he kept his commitment to the Bulldogs when Stansbury was fired and replaced by [[Rick Ray (basketball)|Rick Ray]]. ==College career== As a true freshman in [[2012–13 Mississippi State Bulldogs basketball team|2012–13]], Sword appeared all 32 games for the Bulldogs, starting 30 of them.{{Cite web|url = http://www.hailstate.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205731093&DB_OEM_ID=16800|title = Craig Sword bio|date = |accessdate = May 22, 2015|website = HailState.com|publisher = |last = |first = }} He was named SEC Freshman of the Week twice, and led the Bulldogs with 10.5 points per game. The Bulldogs finished a dismal 4–14 in the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]], however. Sword improved his scoring clip in [[2013–14 Mississippi State Bulldogs basketball team|2013–14]] to 13.7 PPG as a sophomore. Sword scored his career high, 33 points, in a 91–82 loss to LSU.{{Cite web|url = https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400506432|title = Frosh lead LSU past Mississippi State 92-81|date = February 19, 2014|access-date = |website = ESPN.com|publisher = |last = |first = }} Sword was sidelined with a back injury in the first half of his junior year in [[2014–15 Mississippi State Bulldogs basketball team|2014–15]]. However, he returned to full form during the conference portion of the season, again leading the Bulldogs in scoring, leading the Bulldogs to a 6–12 conference record, and a generally much more competitive team. Sword was named Second Team All-SEC for his efforts.{{Cite web|url = http://www.clarionledger.com/story/mississippistatesports/2015/03/10/msu-craig-sword-named-second-team-all-sec/24731173/|title = Craig Sword named second-team All-SEC|date = March 10, 2015|accessdate = |website = ClarionLedger.com|publisher = The Clarion Ledger|last = Bonner|first = Michael}} Sword places ninth on the [[Mississippi State Bulldogs basketball statistical leaders|Bulldogs' career leaderboard]] with 144 steals. ==Professional career== ===Wilki Morskie Szczecin (2016–2017)=== After going undrafted in
